title: Oxidation–reduction and electrochemical cells
summary: Electron bookkeeping, half reactions, electrochemical potentials, Nernst composition corrections and charge/energy accounting with a device-claim audit.

objectives.description: Balance redox reactions in a specified aqueous medium and check charge and atoms.
Derive and apply cell potentials, ΔrG and equilibrium constants with a stated reaction convention.
Use activities in the Nernst equation and interpret concentration cells.
Connect current, charge, stoichiometry and energy while distinguishing thermodynamics from device kinetics.

preparation.description: Cells and electrode roles; distinguish voltage from current

activities.title: Lecture notes and primary reading
activities.instructions: Work through the notes with the assigned source open. Reproduce each worked calculation or derivation on paper, including its assumptions, before reading the next step. Write one question that remains unresolved.

activities.title: Problem sheet: calculation, explanation and transfer
activities.instructions: Attempt the problems independently first. Use one hint at a time if useful, and record which help you used. Show the reasoning that connects the model and its assumptions to each answer; compare the reference only after a substantial attempt.

activities.title: Return without the notes
activities.instructions: On a later study day, close the notes and reconstruct the core relation and its assumptions, then explain the failure case from the last problem. Compare with your saved work and correct one gap. This practice does not itself certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to judge the objectives: explain assumptions, complete the independent calculations and justify the final transfer/synthesis. The final exercise is the recorded checkpoint; its acceptance alone is not a claim that all course outcomes are mastered.

commonMisconceptions.claim: Multiplying a half reaction multiplies its voltage.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Potential is energy per unit charge; both energy and charge scale, leaving voltage unchanged.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A favourable standard cell must run forward at every composition.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The actual driving force uses Q: E=E°−RT lnQ/(nF).

commonMisconceptions.claim: A positive cell potential guarantees high power.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Equilibrium thermodynamics does not specify current; kinetics and transport constrain power.
